title: Google's AI Buildout Drove a 37% Jump in Electricity Use
hook: Google's own numbers show its electricity use jumped 37% in 2025, driven largely by the data centers behind its AI push — a concrete figure in the debate over AI's energy footprint.
key_points: Google reported its electricity use rose 37% in 2025 compared with the year before.
The increase is tied to the buildout of data centers powering its AI systems.
Google says it's working to balance that growth against clean-energy investments.
It's a concrete number behind a trend already visible in local fights over new data centers.
content_html: Google disclosed that its electricity use climbed 37% in 2025 compared with the prior year, according to Ars Technica — a jump the company attributes largely to the data centers it has been building to power its AI systems.
extra_html: The number puts a concrete figure on a trend this deck has already tracked: AI's usefulness comes with a real electricity and water bill, paid mostly inside the data centers that run it. Google says it's trying to balance that growth against clean-energy commitments, but a 37% jump in a single year is a reminder of how fast AI's physical footprint is scaling alongside the software. It's worth keeping in mind next time a company announces a bigger, more capable model — more capability generally means more compute, and more compute means more power.

related.title: AI's Energy & Water
related.hook: Every chatbot reply runs in a warehouse of power-hungry computers somewhere. AI's convenience has a real physical footprint — in electricity, water for cooling, and carbon.

related.title: Communities Are Pushing Back on AI Data Centers
related.hook: The warehouses that power AI need land, power, and water — and neighbors are starting to say no. New York just signed the nation's first statewide data center ban into law.

flashcards.prompt: By how much did Google's electricity use rise in 2025, and why?
flashcards.back_html: About 37% year-over-year, driven mainly by the data centers built to power its AI systems.

flashcards.prompt: What is Google saying it's doing about this rising energy use?

choices.text: Trying to balance the growth against clean-energy investments

flashcards.explanation_html: Google disclosed the number itself and frames it as a tradeoff it's managing with clean-energy commitments, not a problem it's denying.
